findings.what_i_tried: I opened the pipeline for the data engineer role to get through 140 applicants and pick a shortlist.
findings.what_happened: Candidates are listed with a filter by status and a sort by date applied or name only; each row opens one at a time with "Open candidate", and there is no way to shortlist from the list.
findings.problem: With 140 CVs and 20-minute blocks, opening every candidate one by one is far too slow, and I lose my place in the list after a phone call.
findings.suggestion: Let me tick several rows in the list and shortlist them in one step, and remember which candidate I last opened so I return to the same spot.

findings.what_i_tried: I filtered to "meets all must-haves" and wanted to shortlist the ones I trust.
findings.what_happened: Each row says "meets all must-haves", "missing: [criterion]" or "needs human review", and the reason is only on the candidate page.
findings.problem: I tend to trust a green "meets" without opening the reason, so a wrong result goes straight into my shortlist and I cannot see why from the list.
findings.suggestion: Show the one-line reason and the CV sentence it relied on directly in the row, so I can check it without opening the candidate.

findings.screen: US.05 Create role, step 1: job description
findings.what_i_tried: I pasted the job description and typed the title, department, location and closing date.
findings.what_happened: The screen asks for role details and a pasted job description, and I have to go through three steps before the role is saved.
findings.problem: I already have these details in the job description or my ATS, and retyping them makes me give up; I have three open roles this week.
findings.suggestion: Read title, location and closing date from the pasted job description, and let me copy a previous role as a starting point.

findings.what_i_tried: I clicked Accept on the suggested must-haves quickly to move on.
findings.what_happened: Each must-have has Accept, Edit and Delete, and the role cannot be saved with zero must-haves, but nothing tells me what a wrong must-have will do later to the 140 candidates.
findings.problem: I click through confirmation steps fast and do not know what the AI does, so a wrong must-have such as the years of experience could silently mark good people as missing.
findings.suggestion: Before saving, show a short summary saying how many of the already imported candidates would be marked missing for each must-have, so I notice a bad one.

findings.what_i_tried: I uploaded my CSV export of 140 applications from the ATS.
findings.what_happened: "Check file" lists rows with missing columns, then I press "Import" for valid rows only and then "Run screening" as a separate step.
findings.problem: The invalid rows are left out, and I do not know how I would get those applicants back in; four separate steps with nothing saying where I am in them.
findings.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
findings.suggestion: Let me fix or download the rejected rows right on that screen and re-import them, and show a progress line like "132 of 140 imported, 8 need fixing".

findings.what_i_tried: I looked at a candidate to shortlist them or mark them unsuccessful.
findings.what_happened: The page has the claims, the CV text, an AI toggle, the screening reasons and the history, with Shortlist, Mark unsuccessful and Undo.
findings.problem: That is a lot of material for each of 140 people; I do not understand "Show what was sent to the AI", and I am not told what "Undo" can undo once feedback is drafted or sent.
findings.suggestion: Show the result and reasons first with the other parts collapsed, and say next to Undo what it does and until when.

findings.screen: US.13 Feedback for an unsuccessful candidate
findings.what_i_tried: I wanted to send feedback to many people who were not taken forward in one go.
findings.what_happened: Each draft is edited and approved with "Approve and send" for one candidate at a time, and the text is in English with an English example.
findings.problem: Applicants in Valencia mostly write in Spanish, and approving dozens of messages one by one costs me an afternoon; I also may click Approve too fast.
findings.suggestion: Let me choose the message language per role and approve a batch of similar drafts after reading one example and a list of who will receive it.

findings.screen: US.11 Proof of claims (on the candidate)
findings.what_i_tried: After a phone call I wanted to know which shortlisted candidates still owe me proof before Friday.
findings.what_happened: Proof states are shown on each candidate, and the dashboard only shows counts per role and no names.
findings.problem: I have to open candidate after candidate to find who is waiting, and I cannot see overdue items in one place.
findings.suggestion: Add one list for the role of shortlisted candidates with each item's state and days since the request, so I see who needs chasing.

findings.what_i_tried: I opened the pipeline for the data engineer role to work through 140 applicants and pick a shortlist.
findings.what_happened: Rows show 'meets all must-haves', 'missing: [criterion]' or 'needs human review', sorted only by date applied or name, with 'Open candidate' as the only action.
findings.problem: I have to open each of 140 candidates one by one to shortlist, and after a phone call I lose my place in the list with no marker of who I already reviewed.
findings.suggestion: Let me tick several rows (for example all 'meets all') and shortlist them in one step, and keep a 'reviewed' mark and my scroll position when I come back.

findings.what_i_tried: I filtered by 'meets all must-haves' and read the green result to decide quickly.
findings.what_happened: The row only shows the overall result; the reason and the CV sentence are only in US.10 after opening the candidate.
findings.problem: I tend to trust a green 'meets' without opening it, so I may shortlist someone whose 'meets' rests on a wrong reading, and I cannot tell without extra clicks.
findings.suggestion: Show the one-line reason and the CV sentence under each result in the list, so I can check it without leaving the page.

findings.what_i_tried: I clicked 'Shortlist' and then moved fast to the next candidate.
findings.what_happened: Shortlist, 'Mark unsuccessful' and 'Undo' sit on the same screen next to the screening; 'missing' candidates need a written reason.
findings.problem: I click through confirmations quickly, so I could mark someone unsuccessful by mistake, which starts a feedback message, and I do not know how long 'Undo' works or whether it stops a draft.
findings.suggestion: Make 'Mark unsuccessful' a separate, clearly labelled step that says what happens next, and state that Undo works until I approve and send.

findings.screen: US.05 Create role, step 1: job description
findings.what_i_tried: I pasted the job description and clicked 'Suggest must-haves'.
findings.what_happened: I must also type title, department, location and closing date by hand, then go through accepting or editing each suggestion in US.06 and tick proof items again in US.07.
findings.problem: The job description already has most of this and I run three roles this week; retyping or re-confirming what is already written makes me give up on the tool.
findings.suggestion: Fill title, location and dates from the pasted text, and offer 'Accept all' for must-haves with a single review screen instead of three steps.

findings.what_i_tried: I tried to upload the 140 CVs and run screening within my 20 minutes.
findings.what_happened: I choose files or a CSV, press 'Check file', then 'Import' only the valid rows, then 'Run screening'; there is no mention of how long screening takes or progress.
findings.problem: I do not know if 140 CVs will finish before my next interview, whether I can close the tab, or what happens to the rows with errors.
findings.suggestion: Show a progress count ('62 of 140 screened'), say it keeps running if I leave, and notify me when it is done.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked at the suggested must-haves and the blocked sentences to decide what to accept.
findings.what_happened: Types are written as 'years of experience', 'required skill' and so on, and some sentences are shown as blocked with a reason.
findings.problem: I do not know what the AI does underneath, so I cannot tell how it decides 'needs human review' versus 'missing', and I do not trust a screening I cannot explain to a hiring manager.
findings.suggestion: Add a short plain-language note beside each result on what 'needs human review' means and what the system looked for, with a Spanish option.

findings.screen: US.13 Feedback for an unsuccessful candidate
findings.what_i_tried: I wanted to approve the rejection drafts for many candidates at once on Friday.
findings.what_happened: Each draft is edited and approved one at a time with 'Approve and send'; a blocked draft shows a safety-check result.
findings.problem: With dozens of rejections this is slow, and when a draft is blocked I am not told which phrase caused it or how to fix it; also my candidates may be Spanish speakers.
findings.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
findings.suggestion: Highlight the exact phrase that triggered the block with a suggested fix, allow reviewing similar drafts together, and let me choose the language of the message.

findings.screen: US.11 Proof of claims (on the candidate)
findings.what_i_tried: I wanted to send the proof requests to everyone shortlisted before Friday.
findings.what_happened: Proof items are shown per candidate, and sending of the request email (US.20) is not described as an action anywhere in the situations.
findings.problem: My goal is to send proof requests, but I cannot see where I preview, confirm and send them to a group, or where I see who has not yet replied.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Add a 'Send proof requests' step on the pipeline for all shortlisted candidates, with a preview of the email and a list of who has replied.

findings.what_i_tried: I opened the dashboard to get the best three candidates for the data role to show the CEO.
findings.what_happened: It shows counts per role and stage, missing must-haves and process figures, with no candidate names and no ranking.
findings.problem: I cannot get the one answer I came for, and nothing on the screen says why there is no top three, so I give up.
findings.suggestion: Add a short line on the dashboard: 'We do not rank candidates. Open the shortlisted list for the role', with a link to that list.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked for a single figure that proves hiring got faster.
findings.what_happened: Median days from shortlist to interview-ready is under 'Process figures' per role, with no comparison to before and no overall number.
findings.problem: I need one headline number and a before/after for the CEO, and I do not know which of these figures to quote.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Put a top summary: median days to interview-ready across all roles, with the change against the previous period.

findings.what_i_tried: I read 'Open roles by stage' as showing which role has the best candidates.
findings.what_happened: It shows counts per stage adding up to total applications, with no explanation of what a count means.
findings.problem: I read a high interview-ready count as quality, and I would tell the CEO something misleading.
findings.suggestion: Label the counts 'number of candidates at this stage, not a measure of quality' next to the chart.

findings.what_i_tried: I tried to edit a candidate or change their status myself.
findings.what_happened: As HR lead I am read-only on candidates, and the actions 'Shortlist', 'Mark unsuccessful' and 'Correct claims' are described for recruiters.
findings.problem: I assume I can edit, and I do not know whether the buttons are hidden, greyed out or give an error.
findings.suggestion: Show a banner 'You have view-only access. Ask a recruiter to make changes', and show the action buttons greyed out.

findings.what_i_tried: I tried to sort candidates by best fit to find the top three.
findings.what_happened: Sorting is by date applied or name only, and the filter 'meets all must-haves' gives an unordered list.
findings.problem: With a long 'meets all' list I have no way to pick three, and I will ask for a fit score that does not exist.
findings.suggestion: Offer a 'Shortlist for the CEO' view of shortlisted candidates, with a plain sentence on why each is there, with no score.

findings.what_i_tried: I tried to open the dashboard on my phone between meetings.
findings.what_happened: Four separate blocks (roles, stages, missing must-haves, process figures) plus 'Open verification queue' are on one screen.
findings.problem: It needs explaining and scrolling, and I want one screen in five minutes.
findings.suggestion: Show one summary card per role at the top, with the detail blocks collapsed below.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked for a way to share or export the figures for the CEO.
findings.what_happened: The actions listed are 'open a role's pipeline' and 'Open verification queue' only.
findings.problem: I must screenshot it into a slide, which is slow and may show the wrong date range.
findings.suggestion: Add an 'Export summary (PDF)' button on the dashboard.

findings.what_i_tried: I opened the dashboard to get one answer for the CEO: did hiring get faster?
findings.what_happened: It shows counts per stage and 'Process figures' per role (median days from shortlist to interview-ready), with no comparison to before and no single overall number.
findings.problem: I cannot say 'hiring is faster' to the CEO; I only see per-role medians with nothing to compare against, so I would stop using it.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Put one headline at the top, such as median days from application to interview-ready across all roles, with this quarter against last quarter.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked at 'Open roles by stage' to see which roles are doing well.
findings.what_happened: The stage counts add up to total applications and look like a funnel.
findings.problem: I read big numbers in later stages as better candidates or a better role, and nothing tells me they only count where people are in the process.
findings.suggestion: Add a short line under the stage chart saying it counts where candidates are in the process and is not a measure of quality.

findings.what_i_tried: I wanted the best three candidates for the data role and looked for a sort by best match.
findings.what_happened: I can sort only by date applied or name; rows say 'meets all must-haves', 'missing: [criterion]' or 'needs human review'. The product says it has no rank.
findings.problem: I have no way to get my three names, and it never explains why, so I think the tool is broken.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Add a filter 'Meets all must-haves + proof verified' with a plain line: 'We do not rank people; here are the candidates who passed every check.'

findings.what_i_tried: As HR lead I opened a candidate and tried to shortlist someone or fix a claim.
findings.what_happened: The structure says HR lead is read-only on candidates, but the situation lists Shortlist, Mark unsuccessful and Correct claims with no mention of what I see.
findings.problem: I assume I can edit, so I would click buttons that are missing or disabled and not know why.
findings.suggestion: For HR lead accounts, show a visible 'View only: ask a recruiter to change this' note and hide or grey out the action buttons.

findings.what_i_tried: I opened a candidate to check them quickly in a meeting.
findings.what_happened: The page has claims beside CV text, a toggle for what was sent to the AI, a per-must-have breakdown with sentences, the years working and a History.
findings.problem: It is far too much for a 5-minute look; I would say no to a screen that needs explaining.
findings.suggestion: Open with a three-line summary (must-haves met, proof state, next step) and fold the CV text, AI toggle and history away by default.

findings.what_i_tried: I wanted to know how many shortlisted people are ready for interview and who is holding things up.
findings.what_happened: Proof status is per item on each candidate, and the queue is where work happens; the dashboard gives only a response rate per role.
findings.problem: I cannot see at a glance who is stuck, so I cannot tell the CEO what is slowing hiring down.
findings.suggestion: Add to the dashboard a 'Waiting on proof' count per role with the days waited, linked to the queue.

findings.what_i_tried: On my phone I opened the dashboard to show the figures in a meeting.
findings.what_happened: The structure says nothing about how the dashboard works on a phone or whether I can export or share it.
findings.problem: I need something I can put in front of the CEO, and I cannot see a way to print or send these figures.
findings.suggestion: Add an 'Export summary (PDF)' button on the dashboard and make it readable on a phone.

findings.what_i_tried: I tried to sign in as HR lead to check the tool once a week.
findings.what_happened: Sign in shows email, password and 'Forgot password?'; an account still waiting for a password says to use the invitation link, which only a recruiter can reissue.
findings.problem: If my invitation expires I have to ask a recruiter to get back in to my own budget tool, and I would give up.
findings.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
findings.suggestion: On the expired-link message, add a button 'Email my recruiter for a new invitation' that sends the request for me.

findings.what_i_tried: I opened the email on the bus and tried to decide whether it is a scam before tapping the link.
findings.what_happened: It says who is asking (company and recruiter name), that I was shortlisted, the items, and a secure link with an expiry date, but nothing says what happens to my documents or how to check the request is real.
findings.problem: I have been asked for documents by scam recruiters, so without a privacy statement or a way to verify I stop before I even reach the upload page.
findings.suggestion: Put one plain line in the email, such as 'Your files are seen only by the recruiter at [company] and deleted after 30 days', plus the job title I applied for and a contact address I can reply to.

findings.what_i_tried: I tried to upload a photo of my degree certificate from my phone camera and my GitHub link.
findings.what_happened: The page lists accepted file types and a size limit, but there is no way to see what I picked before it counts, and a 'Replace file' option exists only 'before review'.
findings.problem: I often photograph the wrong page, and once the recruiter starts review I cannot fix it, and I would not know when that happens.
findings.suggestion: Show a preview of the chosen file with 'Use this file' or 'Choose another', and say clearly when replacing is no longer possible.

findings.what_i_tried: After uploading I wanted to know whether the file was really sent so I could close the page.
findings.what_happened: Each item has a status (requested / received / verified), but nothing says a confirmation is shown right after upload or that I get an email receipt.
findings.problem: I am tired and unsure whether it went through, so I may upload again or worry all night.
findings.suggestion: After each upload show 'Received 14:32, thank you' and send a short confirmation email listing what has been received and what is still missing.

findings.what_i_tried: I opened the link two days later after sleeping off my night shift.
findings.what_happened: The structure shows an expiry date in the email and a reminder after 3 days, but does not describe what the candidate sees if the link has expired; only the sign-in screen has an expired-link message.
findings.problem: An expired link with no explanation looks broken or fake, and I might lose my chance without knowing who to contact.
findings.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
findings.suggestion: Add a candidate-facing expired-link screen that says the link ended on [date], gives the recruiter's name and email, and offers a button to request a new link.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked for what I should upload for the reference and for GitHub, in my second language when tired.
findings.what_happened: A reference needs the referee's name and work email, but there is no stated explanation of what the referee will be asked, and no hint how to give a GitHub link versus a file.
findings.problem: I do not want to give a former manager's email without knowing what will be sent to them, so I may skip it.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Next to the referee fields, write in simple words what the referee will be asked and that they will only confirm job title and dates.

findings.what_i_tried: I read the page on my 390 px phone to see how much I had to do.
findings.what_happened: The page shows for each item the reason text, accepted types, size limit, privacy note and status all together, with no stated overall progress or deadline.
findings.problem: It is a lot of text for a tired reader, and I cannot see at a glance what is left or by when.
findings.suggestion: Show the deadline at the top with '1 of 3 items done', and fold the file rules and privacy note under a short 'Details' link per item.

findings.what_i_tried: After sending proof I wanted to know what happens next and when I will hear.
findings.what_happened: The journey has no candidate-visible message after proof is received, apart from the status on the upload page, and the only reminder is one email at 3 days that then marks items 'no response'.
findings.problem: If I miss one reminder, my item is marked 'no response' and I would not be told what that means for my application.
findings.suggestion: Tell me in the first email and the upload page how long I have, what happens if an item is late, and send a second warning before an item is marked 'no response'.

findings.what_i_tried: I opened the email on the bus and tried to decide if it is a real request or a scam before clicking the link.
findings.what_happened: It names the company and recruiter, lists the items and shows a secure link with an expiry date, but nothing says who will see my documents or that I should never send anything by reply.
findings.problem: I have been asked for documents by scam recruiters; without a clear who-sees-this line and a way to check it is genuine, I stop before I even open the link.
findings.suggestion: Put one plain sentence in the email: who will see the files, how long they are kept, that nothing is asked by reply or for bank details, and a named contact to check with.

findings.what_i_tried: I tried to upload my degree certificate and my GitHub link as fast as possible.
findings.what_happened: The privacy note on who sees the files is only listed as something shown on the page, and there is no stated way to give a GitHub profile, only 'Upload a file per item'.
findings.problem: If the privacy note is low on the page or small I will not see it and will leave as it looks like a phishing form. A GitHub profile is a link, not a file, and I do not know what to do.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Show the privacy note at the top in two short lines, and give the GitHub item a text box for the profile URL instead of an upload button.

findings.what_i_tried: I photographed my degree certificate and uploaded it, maybe the wrong page.
findings.what_happened: The spec only offers 'Replace file' before review and the status 'received'; there is no preview or check of what I uploaded.
findings.problem: Tired, I may upload the wrong page and not notice; after review starts I cannot fix it and I do not know if a recruiter will tell me.
findings.suggestion: After upload show a preview of the file with the question 'Is this the right page?' and a clear Replace button, and say what happens if review has already started.

findings.what_i_tried: After uploading I wanted to know that it was sent, so I could close the page and sleep.
findings.what_happened: Each item shows status requested / received / verified, but no confirmation message or email receipt is described.
findings.problem: I am often not sure whether a file was sent and may upload twice or worry all night.
findings.suggestion: Show a clear 'Received, thank you' message with the file name and time, and send a short confirmation email.

findings.what_i_tried: Two days later I opened the link from the email.
findings.what_happened: Only an expiry date is shown in the email; no situation covers a candidate opening an expired link, and only one reminder is sent after 3 days.
findings.problem: If the link has expired I land on something undefined, may be marked 'no response' without knowing, and have no way to ask for a new link.
findings.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
findings.suggestion: Add an expired-link page that says it has expired, that nothing is lost, and offers a button to request a new link from the recruiter.

findings.what_i_tried: I wanted to know how long I have left and what is still missing.
findings.what_happened: The reminder is sent once at 3 days and the item is then marked 'no response'; the spec does not say if it states the final deadline.
findings.problem: Working shifts, I may miss the single reminder and be dropped without a second chance or warning.
findings.suggestion: State the exact deadline date and time in both emails and list only the still-missing items with the link.

findings.what_i_tried: I read the page on a 390 px phone in English while tired.
findings.what_happened: The page includes why each item is needed, file types, size limits, privacy note and statuses all together; nothing says how to take a photo or what size my phone photo will be.
findings.problem: A lot of text for a tired reader, and a phone photo may exceed the size limit with no guidance.
findings.suggestion: Keep one short sentence per item, put limits behind a small 'More info', and let me take a photo directly with automatic resizing.

findings.what_i_tried: I wanted to be sure the reference step was something I had to do.
findings.what_happened: For a reference I must give a referee's name and work email, but nothing says the referee will be contacted or what they will be asked.
findings.problem: I would hesitate to give someone else's email without knowing what is shared with them.
findings.suggestion: Add a line: 'We will email your referee to confirm only your job title and dates; they will not be asked for opinions.'

findings.what_i_tried: I read the first sentence of the rejection email on my phone and prepared to reply with a complaint.
findings.what_happened: The email shows the approved text naming the unmet criteria of the role, such as 'your CV shows 3 years', and nothing else is described.
findings.problem: I have 12 years of experience, so if the stated reason looks wrong or generic I assume the AI misread my CV or discriminated against my age, and I go public.
findings.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
findings.suggestion: Quote the exact CV lines the decision relied on, with the working (for example the years added up), in the first lines of the email, so I can see at once whether the reason is true.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked for a way to contest the decision or ask a human to re-check my CV.
findings.what_happened: The email is described as text from the company's sender address; no contest, appeal or correction route is mentioned, and candidates have no accounts.
findings.problem: With no visible way to dispute it, replying angrily or complaining publicly is my only option.
findings.suggestion: Add a clearly labelled 'Ask a person to review this decision' button or link with a named contact and a response time.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked for whether a human or an AI decided about me.
findings.what_happened: Nothing in the email says that a recruiter reviewed and approved the decision or what the AI did.
findings.problem: I assume AI means nobody read my CV, and I suspect age bias, so I do not trust the reason.
findings.suggestion: State in plain words that a recruiter read your CV and confirmed this decision, and that age or other personal characteristics are not used.

findings.what_i_tried: I read the email in English on my phone at lunch and scanned for the reason.
findings.what_happened: The email is one block of text, and the screens do not say it is short, ordered by importance or available in another language.
findings.problem: I read one sentence and stop; if the reason is buried under pleasantries or long text I miss it and get angry.
findings.suggestion: Put the decision and the single main unmet criterion in the first two lines, with detail below and short paragraphs for a phone.

findings.screen: US.13 Feedback for an unsuccessful candidate
findings.what_i_tried: I assumed the message about me would be specific to my CV and not a template.
findings.what_happened: When no unmet criteria are recorded, a neutral message is used, and the draft is limited to criteria recorded as unmet or unverified.
findings.problem: A neutral or generic rejection with no reason is exactly what turns me into a public complaint, and a recruiter might approve it without noticing.
findings.suggestion: Block approval of a neutral message for a candidate who was screened in detail, or force the recruiter to add a concrete, true reason first.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked at what I would have seen if I had been shortlisted, to compare the process I was put through.
findings.what_happened: Rejected candidates see only the email; the page explains each request and why, but there is no equivalent page showing my own screening result.
findings.problem: I cannot check what the system recorded about my CV, so I must trust the sentence in the email.
findings.suggestion: Give rejected candidates a secure link to a short page showing the criteria, what was found in their CV and the working, with a way to flag a mistake.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked for what happens to my data after the rejection.
findings.what_happened: The structure mentions a 30-day retention period in settings and a privacy note on the upload page, but nothing for the rejection email.
findings.problem: As a suspicious candidate I want to know how long my CV is kept and who saw it, and not finding it makes me trust the company less.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Add one line in the email saying how long my data is kept and how to ask for it to be deleted.

findings.what_i_tried: I read the first line of the rejection email on my phone and looked for the real reason I was turned down.
findings.what_happened: The email shows the recruiter-approved text naming unmet criteria, with no stated place for a human name, a statement of who read my CV, or a way to respond.
findings.problem: I assume AI rejected me because of my age and no person read my CV; nothing in the email tells me a recruiter confirmed it, so I reply angrily or complain publicly.
findings.suggestion: Put one sentence at the top: 'A recruiter, [name], reviewed your CV and confirmed this decision', followed by the specific reason.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked for a button or link to contest the decision or ask for a review.
findings.what_happened: The structure lists no contest, appeal or reply route; the email is sent from a sender address and 'no candidate accounts' exists.
findings.problem: With no way to dispute, my only outlet is replying to a possibly unmonitored address or going public.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible 'Disagree with this? Ask a person to re-check' link that reaches a named recruiter and promises a reply within a set number of days.

findings.screen: US.13 Feedback for an unsuccessful candidate
findings.what_i_tried: I read the reason, e.g. 'requires at least 5 years... your CV shows 3 years', to check whether it is true for me.
findings.what_happened: The draft cites only the criterion and the count; the example reason has no pointer to which CV lines were used, and I have 12 years.
findings.problem: If the system miscounted my years, I cannot see how, so a wrong reason looks like bias and I escalate.
findings.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
findings.suggestion: Include in the email the CV lines used and the working (e.g. '2019-2022 + 2022-2025 = 6 years'), plus how to send a correction.

findings.screen: US.13 Feedback for an unsuccessful candidate
findings.what_i_tried: I expected a specific reason about me, since my experience is clearly strong.
findings.what_happened: When no unmet criteria are recorded the candidate gets a neutral message.
findings.problem: A neutral, generic message after 12 years of experience reads as hiding the real reason, which I treat as proof of age discrimination.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Block approval of a neutral message unless the recruiter adds a plain, true reason, such as 'other candidates matched more of the must-haves' with which ones.

findings.what_i_tried: I looked for whether the email says anything about AI, my data or my rights.
findings.what_happened: The structure shows no statement about AI use, what data was processed, or how to ask for it.
findings.problem: I suspect an automated decision and have no information to confirm or dismiss it, so I assume the worst.
findings.suggestion: Add a short plain note: 'AI flagged items from your CV; a recruiter made the decision', with a link to see what was sent to the AI and request your data.

findings.what_i_tried: I read it on my phone in Polish-speaking mindset, in a quick lunch break, and scanned for the point.
findings.what_happened: The email carries a full approved draft that lists unmet criteria, with no stated length or structure for the reason.
findings.problem: A long block of text means I read one sentence and react to it, probably the opening, which may be generic.
findings.suggestion: Lead with the single main reason in one short line, then details below.

findings.what_i_tried: As a candidate I wondered whether being asked for proof was a fair process, and what happens to my files.
findings.what_happened: There is a privacy note, but nothing connects the upload to a decision or lets me see my status after a rejection.
findings.problem: If I was rejected after providing proof, I have no page to check my status or why, so I feel ignored.
findings.suggestion: Keep the same secure link working to show the final status and the reason message after the decision.
